entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Calrice di Durisio was a renowned physician and medical pioneer of the Classical era, active in Foggia, Italy, from approximately 250 BCE to 200 BCE.\n
Born in the region of Lucania, Calrice di Durisio was a key figure in the development of medical knowledge during the Hellenistic period.\n
He was a prolific writer and made significant contributions to the field of medicine, particularly in the areas of surgery and pharmacology.\n
Calrice di Durisio's work had a lasting impact on the development of medical practices in the Roman Empire, influencing notable figures such as Galen and Hippocrates.\n
Despite the passage of time, Calrice di Durisio's legacy continues to be celebrated by medical historians and scholars, who recognize his pioneering work in the field of medicine.

The Calrice di Durisio's quote: 'Medicine is the art of preserving life,' remains a testament to his enduring contributions to the field.
